day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary Airport at 14:00 on Flight AC. Collect luggage and take the Banff Airporter shuttle (~$60 CAD one-way) to Banff town. Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge. Freshen up and take a leisurely self-guided walk along Banff Avenue to get oriented with the town.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across the free Bow River Bridge and walk the easy, scenic Bow River Trail along the riverbank at no cost. Watch the golden-hour light on the surrounding peaks. Head back to town for dinner.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the Calgary Airport food court before or after baggage claim (~$12-15 CAD)
meals.dinner: Tooloulou's on Bear Street - affordable Cajun-style wraps and bowls, great portions for the price (~$15-18 CAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Banff Airporter shuttle in advance online to secure your seat and potentially save a few dollars. Pick up a free Banff National Park trail map at the Banff Visitor Centre on Banff Avenue before it closes at 17:00. Note: A Parks Canada day pass (~$11 CAD/person) is required to be in the park - consider buying an annual Discovery Pass (~$75 CAD) if you plan to visit other Canadian parks, as it pays off quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike - Catch the free Roam Transit Bus 8X from Banff town centre to Johnston Canyon (departs ~08:30, ~$6 CAD return). Hike the famous catwalk trail carved into the canyon walls to the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km). Arrive early to beat the crowds. The canyon is cool and shaded, perfect for a warm morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue past the Upper Falls on the trail to the Ink Pots - seven colorful cold mineral springs set in an open meadow (~5.8 km one way from trailhead). This hidden gem is far less crowded and rewards the extra effort with stunning views. Bring a packed lunch to eat at the Ink Pots meadow.
day_by_day.evening: Return by Roam Transit bus to Banff. Visit the free Banff Park Museum on Banff Avenue, a National Historic Site with fascinating taxidermy displays of local wildlife (open until 18:00, free admission). Relax and grab dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Pick up supplies from Nesters Market grocery store on Marten Street the night before - pack oatmeal or granola bars to eat at the hotel (~$3-5 CAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Nesters Market - sandwiches, fruit, and trail mix prepared the night before (~$8-10 CAD)
meals.dinner: Banff Ave Brewing Co. - try their affordable pub-style burgers and nachos during happy hour (17:00-18:00) for discounted prices (~$16-20 CAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear layers - Johnston Canyon is noticeably cooler than open trails due to the canyon shade. The catwalk can be slippery near the waterfalls; wear proper hiking footwear. The Ink Pots extension adds ~3 hours but is well worth it for budget travelers as it is completely free and spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek - Book the Parks Canada Moraine Lake shuttle in advance (mandatory reservation system, ~$8 CAD each way from Lake Louise Park & Ride). Depart Banff early by Roam Transit to Lake Louise Park & Ride, then connect to Moraine Lake. Start with the short but rewarding Rockpile Trail (0.8 km) at sunrise for the iconic panoramic view of the Valley of the Ten Peaks and the vivid blue lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return) around the shores of Moraine Lake, taking in close-up views of the turquoise water and towering peaks reflected on the surface. Explore the boulder-strewn shoreline and look for wildlife including pikas and ground squirrels. Eat a packed lunch on the lakeshore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff via shuttle and Roam Transit. Treat yourself to a well-earned soak at the Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$18.50 CAD adult) - a naturally heated mineral pool at 37-40°C with spectacular mountain views. This is a budget-friendly splurge worth every cent after a long hiking day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or pack overnight oats prepared the night before to eat on the bus (~$3 CAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Nesters Market - wraps, cheese, crackers, and energy bars eaten at Moraine Lake shoreline (~$8-10 CAD)
meals.dinner: Melissa's MistSteak on Lynx Street - a Banff institution with hearty portions; order the daily soup and sandwich combo for a budget-friendly meal (~$16-19 CAD)

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake shuttle reservations sell out weeks in advance - book as soon as possible on the Parks Canada reservation website. Arrive at the Rockpile early (before 08:00 if possible) for the best light and fewer crowds. Bring sunscreen and sunglasses as the lake area is very exposed. Bears are frequently spotted in this area - carry bear spray and hike in groups.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike - Take the Roam Transit Bus 8X to Lake Louise (~$6 CAD return). Walk the iconic turquoise shoreline of Lake Louise and continue along the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail past the teahouse viewpoint (10.6 km return). The trail climbs gradually through forest and open moraines with jaw-dropping glacier views. Start early to secure a good position and avoid afternoon heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the historic Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (cash only, ~$8-12 CAD for tea and a scone) - a unique backcountry teahouse that has operated since 1927, powered entirely by glacial water. Continue a short distance further for unobstructed views of the Victoria Glacier before descending back to Lake Louise.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by Roam Transit. Take a free self-guided walk up Tunnel Mountain Trail from town (2.7 km return, ~45 minutes) for panoramic 360-degree sunset views over Banff townsite, the Bow Valley, and surrounding peaks. This is one of the best free viewpoints in Banff.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast from Nesters Market eaten on the bus or at the lake before the hike starts (~$4-5 CAD)
meals.lunch: Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse - a special budget splurge; order tea and a scone or sandwich (cash only, ~$10-14 CAD). Alternatively, bring a packed lunch and eat at the teahouse picnic area for free.
meals.dinner: Nourish Bistro on Bear Street - vegetarian-friendly with affordable Buddha bowls and wraps; one of Banff's best-value sit-down restaurants (~$15-18 CAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Plain of Six Glaciers trail is 10.6 km return with ~365 m elevation gain - wear proper footwear and bring trekking poles if available. Bring cash for the teahouse as they do not accept cards. Lake Louise itself is extremely busy; the early morning start (aim for 07:30-08:00 arrival) ensures a more peaceful experience. The Tunnel Mountain sunset walk takes about 45-60 minutes and is entirely free.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise at Two Jack Lake - Take a short taxi or rideshare (~$15 CAD) to Two Jack Lake, just 13 km from Banff. This stunning, quieter lake offers spectacular reflections of Mount Rundle and is far less crowded than the famous lakes. Walk the easy 4.3 km loop trail around the lake. Look for osprey, bald eagles, and waterfowl. This is a perfect free, low-key morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Fenland Trail (2 km loop, free) near the Forty Mile Creek area on the edge of Banff townsite - a flat, peaceful wetland trail through dense spruce forest excellent for wildlife spotting including beavers and deer. Afterward, visit the free Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies on Bear Street (suggested donation $10 CAD) to learn about the history, art, and culture of the Rockies.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the free Cave and Basin National Historic Site grounds at dusk (exterior viewing is free; interior tours ~$8 CAD). The warm sulphur springs and historic bathhouse are fascinating. Watch for the endangered Banff Springs Snail in the warm outflow streams. Stroll back along the Bow River for a relaxing end to the day.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel - pick up yogurt, fruit, and granola from Nesters Market the day before (~$5 CAD)
meals.lunch: Picnic at Two Jack Lake - pack sandwiches and snacks from Nesters Market (~$8-10 CAD). Enjoy lunch with a view of Mount Rundle.
meals.dinner: Bear Street Tavern - wood-fired pizzas with generous toppings at reasonable prices; great atmosphere and good value for Banff (~$16-20 CAD)

day_by_day.notes: Two Jack Lake is a hidden gem that most tourists skip in favor of Lake Louise and Moraine Lake - take advantage of the relative quiet. The Fenland Trail is stroller and wheelchair accessible, entirely flat, and excellent for wildlife photography in the early afternoon light. If budget allows, the Cave and Basin interior tour ($8 CAD) is well worth the cost for its fascinating history as the birthplace of Canada's national park system.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike up Sulphur Mountain via the Sulphur Mountain Trail (11 km return, ~655 m elevation gain, free) - a challenging but immensely rewarding hike to the summit boardwalk at 2,451 m. The trail winds through dense forest and opens to sweeping views of six mountain ranges. Start no later than 07:00 to enjoy the summit before crowds arrive via the gondola.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free Sanson's Peak Meteorological Station at the summit boardwalk and enjoy 360-degree views. Descend via the gondola if legs are tired (~$65 CAD, optional splurge) or hike back down for free. Back in town, do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Banff Avenue shops - look for affordable local items like postcards, fridge magnets, and locally made jams at reasonable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Banff followed by a peaceful sunset walk along the Bow River Pathway. Pack bags for departure. Arrange the Banff Airporter shuttle back to Calgary Airport for your onward journey.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-hike breakfast - pack overnight oats and a banana to eat at the trailhead before ascending (~$3-4 CAD)
meals.lunch: Summit picnic at Sulphur Mountain - pack a celebratory final-day lunch with good snacks from Nesters Market (~$10-12 CAD). Eat with panoramic mountain views.
meals.dinner: Balkan Restaurant on Banff Avenue - a long-standing Banff budget favorite serving generous Greek and Canadian dishes at some of the most affordable prices in town (~$14-18 CAD). Perfect farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: The Sulphur Mountain hike is the most physically demanding of the trip - save it for the last full day only if legs are still fresh after five days of hiking; otherwise swap with the Day 5 itinerary. The gondola descent ($65 CAD) is a worthwhile splurge on the final day as a treat. Book the Banff Airporter return shuttle at least 24 hours in advance. Leave a buffer of at least 3.5 hours between your Banff departure and any flight from Calgary Airport.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 14:00. Travel time from Calgary Airport to Banff is approximately 1.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary Airport at 14:00, collect luggage, and arrange ground transportation (shared shuttle or rental car recommended). Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge upon arrival (~15:30–16:00). Take a leisurely orientation stroll along Banff Avenue to get acquainted with the town, browse local shops, and visit the Bow River Falls viewpoint — a short, easy 10-minute walk from the main strip.
day_by_day.evening: Explore downtown Banff at dusk. Walk across the Bow River Bridge for golden-hour views of Cascade Mountain, then settle in for a relaxed first dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and snack at Calgary Airport before or after landing.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick bite at a café on Banff Avenue upon arrival — try Whitebark Café for sandwiches and locally roasted coffee.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bison Restaurant & Terrace — mid-range Canadian cuisine featuring locally sourced bison, elk, and seasonal produce. Mains ~CAD $28–40.

day_by_day.notes: Do not over-plan Day 1. The drive from Calgary is scenic but tiring after a flight. Purchase a Parks Canada Discovery Pass at the park gate or online before arrival to cover daily entry fees (~CAD $72.25/adult for an annual pass, well worth it over 6 days).

day_by_day.morning: Banff Gondola Summit Ride & Sulphur Mountain Walk — Take the Banff Gondola from the lower terminal (10 minutes from the hotel) to the summit of Sulphur Mountain at 2,281 metres. Enjoy panoramic views of six mountain ranges and the Bow Valley. Walk the 1 km interpretive boardwalk along the ridge to Sanson's Peak weather observatory. Allow 2–3 hours total. Book gondola tickets in advance online (~CAD $65/adult).
day_by_day.afternoon: After descending, visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs for a relaxing soak in the natural thermal mineral pools at 1,585 metres elevation — the perfect recovery after the morning's altitude. (~CAD $16/adult, towel rental available). Spend 1–1.5 hours here before heading back to the hotel to freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Bow River Trail from the hotel area for a peaceful evening nature stroll. Watch for elk grazing near the river banks — common in summer evenings. End the evening with dinner near Banff Avenue.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Tooloulou's on Bear Street — hearty eggs Benedict and French toast options, ~CAD $15–22.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the Banff Gondola summit Sky Bistro café, or pack a light lunch to enjoy at the summit viewpoint.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Coyotes Southwestern Grill — vibrant, flavourful Southwestern-inspired dishes with vegetarian-friendly options. Mains ~CAD $22–35.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the Banff Gondola early (by 9:00 AM) to beat midday crowds. The summit can be cooler and windier than the town below — bring a light layer. The hot springs are a great afternoon complement to the morning's activity.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake — Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek — Depart hotel by 7:00 AM. Note: Private vehicles are restricted from Moraine Lake Road; take the Parks Canada shuttle from Banff or Lake Louise Ski Area (book in advance at reservation.pc.gc.ca, ~CAD $10 each way). Hike the Rockpile Trail (20 minutes, stunning elevated viewpoint) and then the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return, easy, ~1 hour) along the impossibly blue glacial lake framed by ten dramatic peaks. Arrive early to experience the lake before crowds peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the return shuttle to Lake Louise village. Stop at the Lake Louise Visitor Centre to learn about the area's geology and wildlife. Browse the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise gift shop or enjoy a coffee on the lakeside terrace before heading back to Banff (~45-minute drive or shuttle).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Banff town. Visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies for a 1-hour cultural stop (open until 5 PM, ~CAD $12), then enjoy dinner and an evening walk.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the 7:00 AM departure — pack a trail snack and water for the hike.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch enjoyed at Moraine Lake shoreline, or grab a casual bite at the Lake Louise Trading Post Deli (~CAD $12–18).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Saltlik Steakhouse on Banff Avenue — quality Alberta beef steaks and shared plates in a lively atmosphere. Mains ~CAD $30–50.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake shuttle reservations are essential and sell out weeks in advance — book as early as possible. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and layers. The water temperature is glacial; swimming is not recommended. Wildlife sightings (ground squirrels, Clark's nutcrackers) are common along the lakeshore.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike — Drive or take a local shuttle ~20 km west of Banff to Johnston Canyon. Follow the iconic catwalk trail bolted into the canyon walls to the Lower Falls (1.1 km, 30 minutes) and continue to the dramatic Upper Falls (2.7 km from trailhead, ~1.5 hours total). The canyon is cool and shaded — ideal for a warm day. Optional extension: continue 3 km further to the Ink Pots (colourful mineral springs) for a more immersive half-day hike (total ~5.5 km one way).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff and spend the afternoon at Vermilion Lakes — a scenic 5 km (one way) flat, easy trail or cycling path just west of town. Exceptional views of Mount Rundle reflected in the calm wetland lakes. High chance of spotting beavers, herons, and waterfowl. Rent a bike from Bactrax Rentals (~CAD $15/hour) for a relaxed afternoon ride.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset view from the Tunnel Mountain Trail — a short 2.3 km hike (45 minutes) from the hotel area with sweeping panoramic views of the Bow Valley at golden hour. Return for a well-earned dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or grab a coffee and pastry from Wild Flour Artisan Bakery on Bear Street — excellent baked goods.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Johnston Canyon trailhead picnic area, or eat at the Johnston Canyon Resort dining room (~CAD $15–25).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Block Kitchen & Bar — modern Canadian comfort food, craft cocktails, great ambiance. Mains ~CAD $22–38.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon gets very busy by mid-morning — aim to arrive by 8:30–9:00 AM. The catwalk can be slippery near the falls; wear shoes with grip. The Ink Pots extension adds ~2 hours but is highly rewarding and less crowded than the lower canyon.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Guided Wildlife & Glacier Tour — Join a full-day guided tour departing Banff (~7:30–8:00 AM). Travel the legendary Icefields Parkway (Highway 93), one of the world's most scenic drives. Stops typically include Bow Lake, Peyto Lake viewpoint (stunning turquoise teardrop-shaped lake), and the Columbia Icefield. Walk on the Athabasca Glacier with the guide or take an Ice Explorer vehicle ride (~CAD $65 add-on). Keep eyes open for wildlife: bears, elk, bighorn sheep, and mountain goats are frequently spotted along the parkway.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided tour with afternoon stops at Sunwapta Falls and Athabasca Falls — two powerful and accessible waterfalls. The guide will provide geological and ecological context throughout. Return to Banff by approximately 18:00–19:00.
day_by_day.evening: Light evening given the long day. Relax at the hotel, then enjoy a quiet dinner close by.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the tour departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre restaurant (included in some tour packages, or ~CAD $18–25 independently).
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at Banff Ave Brewing Co. — pub-style food, house-brewed craft beers, relaxed atmosphere. Mains ~CAD $18–30.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Icefields Parkway guided tour well in advance through operators such as Pursuit, Brewster Travel Canada, or On the Beaten Path (~CAD $130–180/person depending on inclusions). Wear warm layers — the Columbia Icefield area can be 10–15°C cooler than Banff even in July. This is the longest day of the trip; pace yourself.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike & Plain of Six Glaciers — Depart Banff by 7:30 AM (drive or shuttle to Lake Louise, ~45 minutes). Walk the iconic turquoise shores of Lake Louise along the flat lakeshore trail (4 km return) with the Fairmont Chateau as a backdrop. Continue up the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail (8.6 km one way from the lake, moderate difficulty, ~3 hours up) through ancient moraines to the historic Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse, open seasonally and serving homemade soups, sandwiches, and tea — a quintessential Banff experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the teahouse back to Lake Louise (~2.5 hours). Enjoy a final lakeside moment and take in the views one last time. Drive or shuttle back to Banff by mid-afternoon. Pack bags, check out of the hotel, and begin the ~1.5-hour drive back to Calgary Airport for evening flights, or enjoy a final wander through Banff town if departure allows.
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner in Banff before departure, or dinner at Calgary Airport if time is tight.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before checkout and departure to Lake Louise.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse on the trail — cash only, homemade food, unforgettable setting. (~CAD $15–20). Highly recommended as a trip highlight.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at The Maple Leaf Restaurant on Banff Avenue — upscale-casual Canadian cuisine, wild game, and Pacific seafood. A memorable final meal. Mains ~CAD $30–48.

day_by_day.notes: The Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse is hike-in only and does not take reservations — arrive at the teahouse between 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM for best availability. Bring cash. The full Lake Louise to teahouse and back hike is ~17 km; adjust turnaround point based on energy and departure time. Confirm return transportation to Calgary Airport in advance — allow at least 2.5 hours before flight departure.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight AC arrives at 14:00. Travel from Calgary International Airport to Banff Mountain Lodge (~1.5 hour scenic drive through the Rockies). Private luxury transfer recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge and settle into your suite. Take a leisurely self-guided stroll along the Bow River Trail directly from the hotel to decompress, enjoy the mountain air, and soak in the first views of the Canadian Rockies.
day_by_day.evening: Explore downtown Banff on foot — browse Banff Avenue boutiques and visit the stunning Cascade Gardens overlooking the townsite. Enjoy a welcome dinner at a top Banff restaurant to celebrate the start of the trip.

meals.lunch: N/A — in transit; grab a snack at Calgary Airport or en route
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Maple Leaf Grille & Spirits — iconic Banff fine-dining featuring Canadian wild game, Alberta bison, and an extensive Canadian wine list. Reserve a window table for mountain views.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private luxury airport transfer from Calgary in advance. Upon check-in, ask the concierge to confirm all activity bookings and arrange early-morning vehicle access to Moraine Lake for Day 2 (access is reservation-only). Stay hydrated — altitude in Banff is ~1,383 m and can cause mild fatigue on arrival day.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek — Depart hotel by 6:00 AM to secure your reserved parking or shuttle spot (Moraine Lake access requires advance reservation). Hike the iconic Rockpile Trail for the world-famous panoramic view of the Valley of the Ten Peaks, then descend to the Lakeshore Trail for a full circuit of the impossibly vivid turquoise lake. Allow 3–4 hours total.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the short scenic route to Lake Louise (~15 minutes from Moraine Lake). Enjoy the Lake Louise Shoreline Hike — walk the iconic turquoise shores and continue up the well-maintained trail to the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse for a well-earned rest with glacier views. The teahouse serves light lunches and homemade baked goods.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff for a relaxing evening. Treat yourself to a premium spa treatment at the hotel or visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs — the highest hot springs in Canada — for a soak under the mountain sky.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast or packed breakfast box arranged through Banff Mountain Lodge concierge before 6:00 AM departure
meals.lunch: Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse at the top of the Lake Louise trail — rustic alpine charm with soups, sandwiches, and fresh-baked scones
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eden Restaurant at Rimrock Resort Hotel — Banff's most celebrated fine-dining experience with a tasting menu, sommelier-curated wine pairings, and sweeping Bow Valley views

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake road access is strictly controlled in peak summer — book the Parks Canada shuttle or a private guided vehicle well in advance. Wear sturdy hiking boots and bring layers; even at 25°C in the valley, the lakeshore and upper trails can be cooler. Carry bear spray — this is active bear country.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Guided Wildlife & Glacier Tour — Join a premium full-day guided tour departing Banff early (~7:30 AM). Travel the legendary Icefields Parkway (Highway 93), one of the world's most scenic drives, stopping at Bow Lake and the stunning turquoise Peyto Lake viewpoint. Your expert naturalist guide will identify wildlife including elk, bighorn sheep, mountain goats, and possibly bears or wolves along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north on the Parkway to the Columbia Icefield — walk onto the Athabasca Glacier with your guide or upgrade to an Ice Explorer vehicle excursion onto the glacier surface. Visit the Columbia Icefield Skywalk — a glass-floored observation platform suspended 280 m above the Sunwapta Valley. Begin the scenic return drive south through the Parkway.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by early evening (~6:30–7:00 PM). Enjoy a quiet, indulgent dinner and reflect on a spectacular day of glaciers, wildlife, and mountain grandeur.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed picnic lunch provided by a premium tour operator, enjoyed at a scenic Icefields Parkway viewpoint
meals.dinner: Dinner at Juniper Bistro — a hidden gem with a relaxed upscale atmosphere, locally sourced Alberta ingredients, and a spectacular terrace overlooking the Bow Valley and Mount Norquay

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable premium operator such as Pursuit or a private guided Icefields Parkway tour for the best experience. The full round-trip is approximately 450 km — a full day commitment. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, a warm mid-layer for the glacier, and your camera with extra batteries. Wildlife sightings are most frequent in early morning and late afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike — Drive ~25 minutes west of Banff to Johnston Canyon. Follow the spectacular catwalk trail bolted directly into the canyon walls above the rushing creek to reach the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km). Arrive early (~8:00 AM) to beat crowds and experience the canyon in golden morning light. Optional: continue beyond the Upper Falls to the Ink Pots — seven vivid cold-water springs in an open meadow (~5.8 km one way).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff for a leisurely afternoon. Visit the Banff Gondola Summit Ride & Sulphur Mountain Walk — board the eight-minute gondola ride to 2,281 metres for breathtaking 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges. Walk the Ridgeline Trail along the summit boardwalk to the historic Sanson's Peak Meteorological Station. Spend time at the summit observatory and interpretive centre.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the Sky Bistro atop Sulphur Mountain (accessible via gondola) — one of the most dramatic dining settings in the Canadian Rockies with floor-to-ceiling windows and panoramic mountain views. Alternatively, descend and enjoy a celebratory dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Whitebark Café — Banff's beloved specialty coffee and breakfast spot known for exceptional pastries and eggs; arrive early as it gets busy
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Johnston Canyon Resort patio or a packed gourmet picnic from the hotel concierge enjoyed at the Ink Pots meadow
meals.dinner: Sky Bistro at the top of the Banff Gondola — elevated Canadian cuisine with tableside glacier views; book the window table at sunset for an unforgettable experience

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon is one of Banff's most popular trails — an early start is essential on weekends. The catwalk can be slippery near the falls; appropriate footwear is required. The Banff Gondola last ride down is typically around 9:00–10:00 PM in summer — confirm current operating hours and pre-book gondola tickets online to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise canoe on the Vermilion Lakes — rent a premium canoe or kayak at dawn for a serene paddle on the iconic Vermilion Lakes, just minutes from downtown Banff. The lakes offer some of the most photographed reflections of Mount Rundle in the Canadian Rockies and are a prime wildlife habitat for great blue herons, osprey, beavers, and elk. A peaceful, magical way to spend a morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Minnewanka Lake — the largest lake in Banff National Park. Board a premium Lake Minnewanka boat cruise for a 90-minute guided tour of the dramatic canyon-flanked lake, learning about the submerged ghost town of Minnewanka Landing beneath the surface. After the cruise, enjoy a relaxed walk along the lakeshore trail with stunning mountain reflections.
day_by_day.evening: Indulgent final full-evening in Banff — treat yourself to a premium spa package at Banff Mountain Lodge or the Willow Stream Spa at Fairmont Banff Springs. Then enjoy a grand farewell-style dinner at the iconic Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel.

meals.breakfast: In-room premium breakfast delivered by room service at Banff Mountain Lodge before your early canoe session
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Lake Minnewanka boat cruise dock café, or drive back to Banff for lunch at Crazyweed Kitchen — celebrated for creative globally inspired cuisine using local Rocky Mountain ingredients
meals.dinner: Dinner at 1888 Chop House inside the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel — a legendary steakhouse in a castle-like setting serving prime Alberta beef, fresh seafood, and an award-winning wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Canoe and kayak rentals at Vermilion Lakes should be arranged the day prior through the hotel concierge or a local outfitter. The Minnewanka boat cruise is popular — pre-book online. The Willow Stream Spa at Fairmont Banff Springs is considered one of Canada's finest luxury spas; book treatments at least 2–3 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning hike — Tunnel Mountain Summit Trail, a short but rewarding 2.3 km (one way) hike departing almost directly from downtown Banff. Reach the 1,690 m summit for sweeping views over the Bow Valley, the town of Banff, Mount Rundle, and the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel below. Perfect for a final morning of reflection before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge. Enjoy a leisurely drive back toward Calgary along the Trans-Canada Highway, stopping at the Kananaskis Country viewpoints if time permits. Arrive at Calgary International Airport with ample time for your departure. Private luxury transfer recommended.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary or overnight in Calgary if flight timing requires.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge — full hot buffet or à la carte in the hotel restaurant to fuel your last hike
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Tooloulou's — a beloved Banff institution serving creative Cajun-inspired dishes and brunch items with a warm, vibrant atmosphere; great final Banff meal
meals.dinner: Airport dining or Calgary restaurant if departing late (recommend Charcut Roast House in downtown Calgary for exceptional Alberta charcuterie and farm-to-table cuisine if an overnight is needed)

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 11:00 AM — arrange a late check-out with the hotel if your flight departs in the evening. Luggage can be stored at the hotel while you complete your morning hike. Ensure bear spray is disposed of before the airport as it cannot be taken on flights. Leave enough time for the 1.5-hour Calgary airport transfer and allow extra time for security during peak summer travel season.
